appearanceAtDeliveryLevel.honestNoteOnTheStatedRequirement: The assignment asked that nothing else on the page move except the removed characters. That is not achievable together with a principled fix: removing four characters from a wrapped paragraph either re-wraps it, or else the wrap has to be measured on text that is never drawn. Freezing the wrap to a markup-bearing measurement was rejected — it would leave the renderer laying out forever against characters it does not print, and would let a pair split across two rows be half-removed. So the delimiters are removed BEFORE wrapping, and the movement above is the whole of the consequence; it is reported rather than engineered away.
appearanceAtDeliveryLevel.rasterRead: page 4 of BOTH fixtures rendered locally at 150 dpi with pdftoppm into the scratchpad and read as an image: no asterisk and no underscore anywhere on the page, the five stop conditions read as prose, nothing clipped at any margin and nothing overlapping. Nothing was rastered into the delivered tree and no rasterState was set by it.

whatChanged.atTheCause: The renderer, not the text. sanitizePdfText() — the one funnel every composed page passes through, which already normalises non-breaking spaces, four dash variants, curly quotes, the section sign and the ellipsis — now removes closed markdown emphasis pairs first. The rule itself is one new shared module, scripts/rcap-custom-pleading/composed-page-markdown.mjs, imported by all three renderers rather than copied into any of them.
whatChanged.whyStripAndNotBold: Decided from the composer's own conventions, not invented. These renderers embed exactly ONE face (Times-Roman), draw one drawText per wrapped row and measure every wrap against that one face. Honouring emphasis would mean embedding a second face and splitting the drawn run — a new markup system for pages that have never had one, and it would move the bytes of every family that already ships. So the delimiters are removed, on the same footing as the characters sanitizePdfText already normalises away.
